input_narrative: SYNTHETIC NARRATIVE: Synthetic field service engineering desk reported a routine software validation finding for the atrial fibrillation detection pathway. No confirmatory clinician note is on file, but the automated CI validation gate blocked the release candidate before any clinical deployment, so no patient was exposed regardless. No patient-facing exposure occurred and the engineering finding was fully contained pre-release or resolved as a non-event.

evidence_links.relevance_note: Defines design controls for devices with software, but is not triggered by this contained event.
Relates to software lifecycle, but the finding was contained before deployment.

risk_report.rationale: The incident narrative describes a software validation finding within the atrial fibrillation detection pathway that was blocked by an automated CI validation gate before any clinical deployment. This containment prevented patient exposure and ensured no clinical alert was missed. While the finding represents a technical quality issue, it did not result in harm or potential harm to patients due to the effectiveness of the pre-release controls. The incident does not trigger obligations under EU MDR Annex I, Section 17.1 (electronic programmable systems) or Section 17.2 (software lifecycle), as these sections pertain to design and development processes for devices incorporating software, but the finding was contained before deployment. Similarly, it doesn't necessitate review under 21 CFR § 820.10(c) because no patient-facing exposure occurred.
